\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Monomial under global sign reversal]
\lean{FABL.monomial_neg_input}
\label{FABL.monomial_neg_input}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinate indices, and let
$x$ be a vector of $n$ signs. Reversing every sign in $x$ multiplies the monomial
indexed by $S$ by $(-1)^{|S|}$, where $|S|$ is the number of indices in $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing even Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_odd_of_even_card}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_odd_of_even_card}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_neg_input}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube satisfying
$f(-x)=-f(x)$ for every $x$, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates of even cardinality.
Then the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

Let $n\ge 0$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
that is invariant under every permutation of its coordinates. For any coordinate sets
$S$ and $T$ with $|S|=|T|$, the Fourier coefficients of $f$ at $S$ and $T$ are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Middle layer indicator]
\lean{FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
\label{FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.positiveCoordinateCount}
For a natural number $m$ and a sign vector $x\in\{−1,1\}^{2m}$, the middle layer
indicator is $1$ if exactly $m$ coordinates of $x$ are positive, and is $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Negative coordinates on the middle layer]
\lean{FABL.middleLayerIndicator_eq_one_iff_negative_count}
\label{FABL.middleLayerIndicator_eq_one_iff_negative_count}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.middleLayerIndicator, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount, FABL.positiveCoordinateSet}
\difficulty{5}
For every natural number $m$ and every point $x$ in the sign cube of dimension $2m$, the
middle-layer indicator equals $1$ if and only if exactly $m$ coordinates of $x$ equal
$-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetry of the middle-layer indicator]
\lean{FABL.middleLayerIndicator_isSymmetric}
\label{FABL.middleLayerIndicator_isSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsSymmetric, FABL.middleLayerIndicator, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_permuteInput}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $m$, the indicator of the middle layer in the sign cube of
dimension $2m$ is invariant under every permutation of its coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean sum over the true value]
\lean{FABL.sum_bool_filter_true_middleLayer}
\label{FABL.sum_bool_filter_true_middleLayer}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative extended real number $p$, the sum over the true element of the
Boolean set, restricted to the Boolean value that is true, of the weight that is $p$ at
true and $1-p$ at false equals $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean sum over the false value]
\lean{FABL.sum_bool_filter_false_middleLayer}
\label{FABL.sum_bool_filter_false_middleLayer}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For every nonnegative extended real number $p$, the sum over the false element of the
Boolean set, restricted to the Boolean value that is false, of the weight that is $p$ at
true and $1-p$ at false equals $1-p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of retaining a sign]
\lean{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_self_middleLayer}
\label{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_self_middleLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF, FABL.correlationKeepProbability, FABL.sum_bool_filter_true_middleLayer}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $p=(1+\rho)/2$. For any sign $x\in\{−1,1\}$, the coordinate
noise distribution with parameter $\rho$, started at $x$, assigns probability $p$ to
$x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of flipping a sign]
\lean{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_neg_middleLayer}
\label{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_neg_middleLayer}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF, FABL.correlationKeepProbability, FABL.sum_bool_filter_false_middleLayer}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $p=(1+\rho)/2$. For any sign $x\in\{−1,1\}$, the coordinate
noise distribution with parameter $\rho$, started at $x$, assigns probability $1-p$ to
$-x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise from the positive sign]
\lean{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_one_toReal}
\label{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_one_toReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_neg_middleLayer, FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_apply_self_middleLayer, FABL.correlationKeepProbability_le_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and $y\in\{−1,1\}$. Under coordinate noise with parameter $\rho$,
started at $1$, the probability of output $y$ is $(1+\rho)/2$ if $y=1$, and $(1-\rho)/2$
otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise mass on the middle layer]
\lean{FABL.noiseKernel_allOne_middleLayer_mass_toReal}
\label{FABL.noiseKernel_allOne_middleLayer_mass_toReal}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.coordinateNoisePMF_one_toReal, FABL.independentProductPMF_apply, FABL.middleLayerIndicator, FABL.middleLayerIndicator_eq_one_iff_negative_count, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount, FABL.positiveCoordinateSet}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $y\in\{-1,1\}^{2m}$ have
exactly $m$ positive coordinates. The noise kernel at the all-positive vector assigns
$y$ probability whose real value is
$\left(\frac{1+\rho}{2}\right)^m\left(\frac{1-\rho}{2}\right)^m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the middle layer]
\lean{FABL.sum_middleLayerIndicator}
\label{FABL.sum_middleLayerIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.middleLayerIndicator, FABL.signCubeEquivFinset, FABL.signCubeEquivFinset_apply_card}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $m$, the sum over all sign vectors $x\in\{-1,1\}^{2m}$ of
the indicator that exactly $m$ coordinates of $x$ equal $1$ is $\binom{2m}{m}$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $m$ and real $\rho$, let $f$ be the indicator of the
middle layer of $\{−1,1\}^{2m}$, consisting of points with exactly $m$ positive
coordinates. The noise operator applied to $f$, evaluated at the all-one point, equals
$\displaystyle\sum_{U\subseteq[2m]}\widehat f(U)\rho^{|U|}$, where $\widehat f(U)$ is
the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.noiseOperator_middleLayerIndicator_allOne_eq_fourierSum}
  {direct}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b003}
\difficulty{5}
For every nonnegative integer $m$, real $\rho$, and sequence $(T_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ of
subsets of $[2m]$ such that $|T_i|=i$ whenever $i\le 2m$, the noise operator applied to
the indicator of the middle layer of $\{−1,1\}^{2m}$, evaluated at the all-one point,
equals $\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{2m}\binom{2m}{i}\widehat f(T_i)\rho^i$, where $\widehat
f(T_i)$ is the Fourier coefficient of that indicator at $T_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Middle layer Fourier polynomial]
\lean{FABL.middleLayerFourierPolynomial}
\label{FABL.middleLayerFourierPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
For a natural number $m$, form a real polynomial by summing over all subsets $U$ of the
$2m$ coordinates: the coefficient of $X^{|U|}$ contributed by $U$ is the Fourier
coefficient of the middle layer indicator at $U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Middle layer binomial polynomial]
\lean{FABL.middleLayerBinomialPolynomial}
\label{FABL.middleLayerBinomialPolynomial}
\leanok
For a natural number $m$, define the real polynomial
$\sum_{j=0}^{m}(-1)^j\binom{m}{j}X^{2j}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the Middle-Layer Fourier Polynomial]
\lean{FABL.eval_middleLayerFourierPolynomial}
\label{FABL.eval_middleLayerFourierPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.middleLayerFourierPolynomial, FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
\difficulty{1}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer, and on the sign cube with $2m$ coordinates let $f$ be
the indicator of vectors having exactly $m$ positive coordinates. For each coordinate
subset $U$, let $\widehat f(U)$ be the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$. For
every real $\rho$, the middle-layer Fourier polynomial evaluated at $\rho$ equals
$\sum_{U\subseteq[2m]}\widehat f(U)\rho^{|U|}$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.middleLayerBinomialPolynomial}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b002}
\difficulty{4}
For nonnegative integers $m$ and any real number $\rho$, define
$P_m(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}(-1)^j\binom{m}{j}X^{2j}$. Then $P_m(\rho)=(1-\rho^2)^m$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$, the Fourier polynomial of the indicator of the middle
layer in the sign cube of dimension $2m$ equals the binomial polynomial
$\sum_{j=0}^{m}(-1)^j\binom{m}{j}X^{2j}$ multiplied by the constant polynomial with
value $\binom{2m}{m}/2^{2m}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Middle-layer Fourier polynomial coefficient]
\lean{FABL.coeff_middleLayerFourierPolynomial}
\label{FABL.coeff_middleLayerFourierPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_of_card_eq_of_isSymmetric, FABL.middleLayerFourierPolynomial, FABL.middleLayerIndicator, FABL.middleLayerIndicator_isSymmetric}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m,k\ge 0$, and let $T$ be a subset of the $2m$ coordinates with $|T|=k$. The
coefficient of $t^k$ in $\sum_{U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2m\}}\widehat{f}(U)t^{|U|}$ is
$\binom{2m}{k}\widehat{f}(T)$, where $f$ is the indicator of sign vectors having exactly
$m$ positive coordinates and $\widehat{f}(U)$ is its Fourier coefficient at $U$.
\end{theorem}

For nonnegative integers $m$ and $j$ with $j\le m$, the coefficient of $t^{2j}$ in
$\sum_{q=0}^{m}(-1)^q\binom{m}{q}t^{2q}$ is $(-1)^j\binom{m}{j}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For nonnegative integers $m,j$ with $j\le m$, let $T$ be a set of coordinates in a cube
of dimension $2m$ with $|T|=2j$. The Fourier coefficient at $T$ of the indicator of
inputs having exactly $m$ positive coordinates is
$(-1)^j\binom{m}{j}\big/\binom{2m}{2j}\;\cdot\;\binom{2m}{m}/2^{2m}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Appending a sign leaves the monomial unchanged]
\lean{FABL.monomial_map_castSucc_snoc}
\label{FABL.monomial_map_castSucc_snoc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a subset of the first $k$ coordinate indices,
let $x$ be a vector of $k$ signs, and let $b$ be another sign. Embed $T$ into the first
$k$ coordinates of a vector of length $k+1$, and append $b$ to $x$; the monomial indexed
by the embedded set at the extended vector equals the monomial indexed by $T$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient under coordinate extension]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_lift_init}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_lift_init}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_map_castSucc_snoc}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $g$ be a real-valued function on the
$k$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $T$ be a finite set of its coordinates. Extend $g$
to the $(k+1)$-dimensional cube by ignoring the last coordinate. The Fourier coefficient
of this extension at the set $T$ embedded among the first $k$ coordinates equals the
Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $T$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b004,

\proofstep
  {FABL.discreteDerivative_majority_odd_last_eq_middleLayerIndicator}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b001}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$, the discrete derivative in the last coordinate of majority
on the $(2m+1)$-dimensional sign cube, viewed as a real-valued function, is the
indicator of the middle layer on the first $2m$ coordinates: it equals $1$ exactly when
those coordinates contain $m$ positive signs, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b001,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer and let $T$ be a finite set of coordinates in
$\{0,\ldots,2m-1\}$. The Fourier coefficient of majority on the $(2m+1)$-dimensional
Boolean cube at the set consisting of the last coordinate together with the coordinates
of $T$ embedded among the first $2m$ coordinates equals the Fourier coefficient at $T$
of the indicator of the middle layer of the $2m$-dimensional cube, namely the inputs
with exactly $m$ coordinates equal to $+1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the real-valued majority function on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is
invariant under every permutation of the input coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oddness of majority]
\lean{FABL.majority_toReal_odd}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b003
}
\label{FABL.majority_toReal_odd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.majority, FABL.majority_odd}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be an odd natural number, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be the majority
function, viewed as real-valued. Then $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for every input $x$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be an odd nonnegative integer and let $S$ be a finite set of coordinates in
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with even cardinality. The Fourier coefficient of the majority
function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube at $S$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-degree majority coefficients]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_majority_two_mul_add_one}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b002
}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_majority_two_mul_add_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_of_card_eq_of_isSymmetric, FABL.fourierCoeff_majority_odd_insert_last, FABL.fourierCoeff_middleLayerIndicator, FABL.majority, FABL.majority_toReal_isSymmetric, FABL.middleLayerIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
For any nonnegative integers $m,j$, let $S$ be a set of coordinates in a cube of
dimension $2m+1$ with $|S|=2j+1$. The Fourier coefficient of majority at $S$ is
$(-1)^j\binom{m}{j}\big/\binom{2m}{2j}\;\cdot\;\binom{2m}{m}/2^{2m}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be odd, let $k$ be odd, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates in
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S|=k$. The Fourier coefficient of majority at $S$ is
$(-1)^{(k-1)/2}\binom{(n-1)/2}{(k-1)/2}\big/\binom{n-1}{k-1}\;\cdot\;2\binom{n-1}{(n-1)/2}/2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[An inverse-square-root inequality]
\lean{FABL.exercise5_24}
\label{FABL.exercise5_24}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ with $1\leq k$ and $2k\leq n$, one has
$\left(1-\frac{k+1}{n}+\frac{k}{n^2}\right)^{-1/2}\leq 1+\frac{2k}{n}$.
\end{theorem}
